cards.back: Yes. A 64-bit OS runs both 64-bit and 32-bit applications. A 32-bit OS can only run 32-bit applications.

cards.front: What is the maximum RAM a 32-bit OS can address?

cards.back: No. Windows 11 is 64-bit only. There is no 32-bit version.

cards.front: Where does Windows store 32-bit and 64-bit apps on a 64-bit system?
cards.back: 64-bit apps: C:\Program Files. 32-bit apps: C:\Program Files (x86).

cards.front: What must match when installing hardware drivers on a 64-bit OS?
cards.back: The driver must also be 64-bit. A 32-bit driver will not work on a 64-bit OS.
GPU built into the same physical chip as the CPU. Saves power and space. Adequate for everyday tasks but insufficient for 3D modeling or video editing.
A separate add-in graphics card installed in the computer. Required for 3D modeling, video editing, and gaming. Installed in desktops.

cards.front: How do you check current free RAM before installing an app?
cards.back: Task Manager (Performance tab > Memory). Shows currently available memory, separate from just total installed.

cards.front: What is a hardware token (dongle) for software licensing?
cards.back: A physical USB device that must be connected for the application to run. The app checks for it at launch. Common for expensive, niche professional software.

cards.front: Why should you install apps from the manufacturer's website rather than a third-party source?
cards.back: Third-party download sites may distribute modified installers containing malware. The manufacturer's site is the trusted source.
A disk image file (ISO 9660 filesystem). Contains an entire folder/filesystem in one file. Mounts as a virtual drive showing all contents. Common for OS installation media.

cards.front: What are OS images (cloning) used for in enterprise deployments?
cards.back: Rapid deployment - create one base image with OS + patches + apps + config, then apply it to many machines. Minutes to deploy vs hours to manually install. Ideal for VMs because virtual hardware is always identical.

cards.front: What rights and permissions does an installed application have?
cards.back: The same rights as the logged-in user who installed it. The app can access any files, shares, and network resources that user can access.

cards.front: Why should organizations test applications in a sandbox before production?
cards.back: An untested app can overwrite files, break existing software, conflict with other apps, or cause system failures. UI changes in upgrades also require workflow updates and retraining.
